extracted.intended_audience: Applicants to the Knight‑Hennessy Scholars (KHS) graduate scholarship program (prospective Stanford graduate students)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and requirements for completing the Knight‑Hennessy Scholars application for the 2026 cohort, including required materials, deadlines, essay prompts, recommenders, and submission policies. Intended to guide applicants through producing a complete and compliant application.

rubrics_metrics.name: KHS application and Stanford graduate degree application both required
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered for selection as a Knight-Hennessy scholar, you must submit an application to Knight-Hennessy Scholars (KHS) and a separate application to the graduate degree program(s) that you wish to pursue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full application instructions are available on our website. You must submit your Stanford graduate degree program application(s) by the program deadline established for Knight-Hennessy Scholars applicants, or December 2, 2025 at 11:59 pm (Pacific Time), whichever occurs first.

rubrics_metrics.name: KHS application deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit all KHS application materials by Wednesday, October 8, 2025 at 1:00 pm (Pacific Time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your recommenders should also submit letters of reference by this deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate degree program application deadline rule
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit your Stanford graduate degree program application(s) by the program deadline established for Knight-Hennessy Scholars applicants, or December 2, 2025 at 11:59 pm (Pacific Time), whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Stanford's Graduate Degree Program page for specific program deadlines; deadlines vary by program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program ineligibility list
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants to certain Stanford graduate degree programs are not eligible for Knight-Hennessy Scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically lists ineligible applicants: Applicants to the Honors Cooperative Program; Master of Liberal Arts; Doctor of Science of Law (JSD) and Master of Legal Studies (MLS); current Stanford students pursuing coterminal graduate study; current Stanford PhD students adding an MA or MS in their current discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and AI prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: All of the information that you provide in this application is expected to be your own work and, to the best of your knowledge, complete and accurate, and that no Artificial Intelligence (AI) language tools including, but not limited to, ChatGPT are used to produce the content of your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your electronic signature affirms this; violations (including misrepresentation or material omission) may lead Stanford to withdraw an offer of admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommenders: number and authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Two letters of recommendation must be submitted by the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your recommenders must be the sole authors of your letters of recommendation. Drafting, writing, translating, or submitting your own letters of recommendation, even if asked to do so by a recommender, is a violation of application terms. Register recommenders early; you may submit your application before letters arrive and monitor status on your status page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommender submission logistics and replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: When you add a recommender the system sends a personalized link; after submission you receive email notification and status updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To change a recommender: click 'Edit' then 'Exclude' (the excluded recommender will not receive a notification). You will then be able to add a new recommender. Your personal message to the recommender will be included in the email notification and displayed on the recommendation form.

rubrics_metrics.name: FERPA waiver choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may waive or not waive the right to access recommendation letters; waiver is optional and recommenders will see the applicant's choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiving or not waiving that right will have no bearing on the handling of your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcripts: which institutions require upload
rubrics_metrics.description: For each institution you list where you have been enrolled full-time in an undergraduate or graduate degree program, upload your transcript if you attended for one academic year or longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transcript may be unofficial or official. The transcript must be in English and indicate the degree conferred and conferral date, if applicable. If you cannot obtain a transcript, you may use the self-reported transcript template; use it if your institution does not provide an English translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcript input exceptions (GPA/rank)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no rank in class indicated on your transcript, then you do not need to enter a rank in class. If there is no GPA indicated on your transcript, then you do not need to enter a GPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate degree program selection limits
rubrics_metrics.description: You may apply to only one Stanford graduate degree program in an application year, with exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: Within the Biosciences, you may select up to two PhD programs; you may apply concurrently to one program listed on the Explore Graduate Programs page and one or more professional school programs (e.g., a PhD and a JD). Refer to scenario-specific instructions (MSTP, Berg Scholars, MBA, Joint MA in Education, current Stanford students, deferred admission applicants). If none apply, list only one program. If you need to change your degree program, delete the existing entry before adding a new program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resume length and content guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Your one-page resume frames your intellectual, personal, and professional background and accomplishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is fine to duplicate information in other sections. If you’ve worked for more than a decade, you may add a page; otherwise limit your resume to one page. Do not include external links on your resume as materials external to your application will not be reviewed. Upload Word or PDF only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work experience entries and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: List up to six internships and work experiences (full-time and part-time) in chronological order, beginning with the most recent experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research experiences can be included in either Employment or Activities. If you want to share more than six, include them under Additional Background. These experiences provide context about your professional path and are opportunities to demonstrate selection criteria. All fields are required for Work Experience entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities: number, order, and detail
rubrics_metrics.description: List up to three activities in order of significance to you, with the most meaningful listed first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include organization/activity name, roles, responsibilities (if applicable), country, city, state, dates, and an order of importance (1-3). If there are additional activities you wish to tell us about, include them on your resume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and honors: number, order, and required explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Add up to three awards or honors in order of significance, with the most meaningful listed first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each award include date received, basis of selection (e.g., criteria, number of recipients, frequency, and who determines recipients, if available), and why the award or honor is meaningful to you. All fields are required to record an award entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized test score policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If your graduate degree program requires test scores, you are required to submit test scores for your Knight-Hennessy Scholars application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any required test scores are due by your graduate degree program's deadline or the KHS deadline, whichever is later. You may submit the KHS application without scores but are encouraged to submit scores early. KHS accepts self-reported scores; you do not need to send official scores to KHS. List all test scores you plan to submit; the admissions committee will see the highest score from each section and, for tests with a total score, the highest total from one sitting. Include English proficiency tests (e.g., TOEFL) if required by your graduate program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language entry limits
rubrics_metrics.description: You may enter a maximum of five languages in the Spoken Languages section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you speak more than five languages, or speak a language not included in the dropdown list, include this information on the Additional Information page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short answers / essay personalness and uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-answer and essay questions invite you to share in your own words what you have done, who you are, and what you aspire to do in the future; 'There are no right answers, topics, or formats — only you can tell your own story.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The strongest responses are so personal to you that no one else could have possibly written them. Write and save your short answers/essay in a separate document, then copy-and-paste. Pay attention to word limits; text boxes will not hold content that exceeds the limit. Avoid non-standard formatting (e.g., excessive line spacing) which will not display properly in the PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essay and short-answer word limits and prompts
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific prompts and word limits: Short Answer 1 — 'Describe your short term and long term academic and professional intentions.' (250 words). Short Answer 2 — prompts about engaging with different perspectives, acting with courage, falling short (combined 250 words). Short Answer 3 — eight improbable facts (combined 150 words). Essay — 'Connect the dots. How have the influences in your life shaped you?' (550 words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text box will enforce the word limits; monitor combined word counts for multi-part prompts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Background disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must answer questions about current Stanford graduate enrollment, previous applications to KHS, personal conduct (suspensions, dismissals, disciplinary actions), academic probation, and gaps (>3 months neither working nor in school).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting 'Yes' to conduct or probation questions does not automatically disqualify you; KHS seeks context. Use the 'Additional Information' space (750 characters) to share essential information not conveyed elsewhere, but do not include essays, recommendation letters, portfolios, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application errors must be corrected before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The system detects missing required fields and errors which must be corrected before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of required field errors are missing birthdate, name, address, legal sex, primary phone, degree program, missing resume, missing recommenders, missing essays, missing short answer responses, and missing conduct/gap questions. The page lists detected errors and potential problems (e.g., missing secondary/high school info, no work experience, no activities, no awards, missing test scores if required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preview PDF requirement and formatting check
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must click 'Preview Application PDF' to generate the PDF that the review committee will see and review the entire application PDF carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that paragraph text responses are displayed in full for Work Experience, Activities, Awards and Honors, Short Answers & Essay, and Additional Background. If responses meet character limits but are cut off, edit to fit within the allotted space — removing line breaks often resolves the issue. Ensure transcripts and resume display correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission edit exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not edit your application after it is submitted, with the following exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may update Test scores, Recommenders, Resume, and Degree Programs on your application status page after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application data ownership, privacy, and sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: By submitting, you consent to Stanford University’s collection and processing of personal data; your application materials and supporting information become the property of Stanford University.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials may be used as part of selection for any Stanford graduate program or for financial support; KHS may share application materials including recommendation letters with Stanford graduate programs if it will aid admission or financial aid efforts. Refer to Stanford privacy policies at privacy.stanford.edu.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to withdraw offer and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Stanford reserves the right to withdraw an offer of admission if you show a significant drop in academic performance or fail to graduate; there has been a misrepresentation or material omission; or pre-attendance behavior indicates a serious lack of integrity or judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stanford may require additional information and/or authorization for the release of information about any such matter. Your electronic signature constitutes consent to verification of information presented in your application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character/field limits for specific entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain fields have explicit character or word-count limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Activities role/description fields show '150 characters remaining'; Awards '300 characters remaining'; Additional Information '750 characters remaining'; Short Answer and Essay fields show specific word limits (250, 150 combined, 550). Follow on-screen counters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on language of transcripts and acceptable alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Transcripts must be in English; if your institution does not provide an English translation, you may use the self-reported transcript template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are unable to obtain an unofficial or official transcript from your institution, you may use the self-reported transcript template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on including external materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include external links on your resume and do not include essays, additional recommendation letters, portfolios, etc., in the Additional Information field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: KHS will not review materials external to your application; Additional Information should be used only for essential contextual information not conveyed elsewhere.
